chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who killed a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram while he was in the Haram and not in the state of ihram.

He said: "Its value is due from him, and it is one dirham, which he gives in charity or uses to buy food for the pigeons of the Haram. But if he killed it while he was muḥrim in the Haram, then a sheep is due from him, along with the value of the pigeon."

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary in which special legal protections apply
key_terms.الْحَمَامَةِ: the pigeon for which the ruling is being given
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: the amount assessed here as one dirham
key_terms.شَاةٌ: a sheep due as sacrificial compensation
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for killing a pigeon in the Haram, whether one is in ihram or not?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning killing a pigeon belonging to the sanctuary of the Haram. If a non-muhrim kills it within the Haram, he must pay its value of one dirham in charity or for feeding the pigeons of the Haram; if a muhrim does so within the Haram, both a sheep and the bird’s value are due.
